# Daily AI Newsletter Digest - 21/2/2026

## 🔥 Top Stories
- Google has released Gemini 3.1 Pro, achieving a 77.1% score on ARC-AGI-2, a benchmark for abstract reasoning and generalization, and outperforming competing models in various benchmarks.
- OpenAI is expanding its presence in India, with plans to partner on data centers, roll out ChatGPT Enterprise, and provide 100,000 Edu licenses, aiming to increase its user base.
- The electric vehicle (EV) industry is facing significant security challenges, with vulnerabilities in authentication, data exchange, and charging infrastructure, and researchers have identified three classes of security risks.

## 🤖 AI Models & Research
- Gemini 3.1 Pro demonstrates improved structured output and code reliability, with cleaner UI layouts and stronger visual hierarchy, and has achieved impressive benchmark numbers, indicating significant improvements in AI performance.
- NotebookLM now features "Prompt-Based Revisions," allowing users to edit slides by simply asking for changes, such as "make slide 3 punchier" or "swap out the chart."
- Researchers have surveyed real-world attacks on EV charging systems, identified systemic weaknesses in widely deployed standards, and mapped out where current defenses are falling short.

## 🛠️ Tools & Products
- Base44 is a tool that allows users to describe an app in plain English and then builds it, with features like UI, database, auth, and hosting, and the ability to iterate and refine until the app meets the user's needs.
- Razer's Project Motoko is an AI headset with dual cameras and always-on microphones, designed as a universal platform that can plug into various AI services.
- Norton Neo, the world's first safe AI-native browser, has been introduced, featuring context-aware AI, privacy, and security, designed to reduce prompting and make AI more accessible.

## 📰 Industry News
- OpenAI's expansion in India includes partnerships on data centers, the rollout of ChatGPT Enterprise, and the provision of 100,000 Edu licenses, aiming to increase its user base and provide more access to AI technology.
- The EV industry's rapid growth has outpaced the development of secure charging infrastructure, creating a need for standardized security protocols, and the Open Charge Point Protocol dominates current implementations but has known vulnerabilities.

## 📚 Resources & Learning
- The World of AI's latest YouTube video discusses Gemini 3.1 Pro and its implications, and the JournalClub.io episode on securing the EV charging ecosystem provides more details on protocol specifications, IDS performance, and suggested strategic framework.
- The Original Paper on securing the EV charging ecosystem can be found at https://journalclub.io/track/EgcQDcyCZAkn1vh83vBAtJAxcvJbmW4LeouRdOL4efOBwk81hc, and JournalClub.io's privacy policy can be found at https://journalclub.io/track/xXDGTFREvRazVYtkXhbVRo9p9G4775BiiCwIJ5BnfLaxBoYbcV.

## TAAFT - There's An AI For That

### Key Highlights
- Google has rolled out Gemini 3.1 Pro, which includes "core intelligence" for complex reasoning tasks and is available across the API, Vertex AI, the Gemini app, and NotebookLM.
- NotebookLM now features "Prompt-Based Revisions," allowing users to edit slides by simply asking for changes.
- OpenAI is expanding its presence in India, with 100 million weekly ChatGPT users, and plans to partner on data centers, roll out ChatGPT Enterprise, and provide 100,000 Edu licenses.
- Base44 is a tool that allows users to describe an app in plain English and then builds it, with features like UI, database, auth, and hosting.
- Razer's Project Motoko is an AI headset with dual cameras and always-on microphones, designed as a universal platform that can plug into various AI services.

### Detailed Points
- Gemini 3.1 Pro boasts impressive benchmark numbers, indicating significant improvements in AI performance.
- NotebookLM's Prompt-Based Revisions enable users to make changes to slides by simply describing the desired edits, such as "make slide 3 punchier" or "swap out the chart."
- OpenAI's expansion in India includes partnerships on data centers, the rollout of ChatGPT Enterprise, and the provision of 100,000 Edu licenses, aiming to increase its user base.
- Base44 allows users to turn their app ideas into reality by describing the app, and it handles the building process, including UI, database, auth, and hosting, with the ability to iterate and refine until the app meets the user's needs.
- Project Motoko by Razer is positioned as an AI headset that might actually work, with features like dual cameras at eye level and far and near-field microphones, seeing and hearing what the user does without needing a phone.
- Other AI tools mentioned include XBert AI for business receptionist tasks, Tavus for real-time AI video avatars, Clipdrop for background removal and image editing, Lucid Engine for tracking how AI search engines see a brand, and GoAI for market scanning and investment alerts.
- A BBC reporter demonstrated a 20-minute hack of ChatGPT by creating a fake webpage and getting AI to echo it back as fact, highlighting the importance of reliable information sources.
- The newsletter also touches on Spot the Fake, a challenge to identify which of two images is AI-generated, and invites readers to participate.

newsletters.subject: Google DROPS Gemini 3.1 Pro
newsletters.summary:
## World of AI Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Google has released Gemini 3.1 Pro, achieving a 77.1% score on ARC-AGI-2, a benchmark for abstract reasoning and generalization.
- Gemini 3.1 Pro outperforms competing models in various benchmarks, including GPQA Diamond, SWE-Bench Verified, BrowseComp, and MCP Atlas.
- The model demonstrates improved structured output and code reliability, with cleaner UI layouts and stronger visual hierarchy.
- Norton Neo, the world's first safe AI-native browser, is introduced, featuring context-aware AI, privacy, and security.

### Detailed Points
- Gemini 3.1 Pro's 77.1% score on ARC-AGI-2 represents a significant improvement in abstract reasoning and generalization capabilities.
- The model's performance on various benchmarks, including:
  * 94.3% on GPQA Diamond, reflecting strong scientific and technical reasoning
  * 80.6% on SWE-Bench Verified, indicating competitive agentic coding ability
  * 85.9% on BrowseComp, suggesting stronger search and tool-grounded reasoning
  * 69.2% on MCP Atlas, evaluating multi-step workflow execution
- Gemini 3.1 Pro's improvements in UI/UX generation, producing more polished UI layouts and cleaner component structuring.
- The strategic implication of Gemini 3.1 Pro's advancements, shifting the focus from conversational fluency to abstract rule induction, long-horizon planning, tool-grounded reasoning, and structured outputs.
- The introduction of Norton Neo, a safe AI-native browser, featuring context-aware AI, privacy, and security, designed to reduce prompting and make AI more accessible.

newsletters.summary:
## JournalClub.io Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- The electric vehicle (EV) industry has seen a significant surge, with nearly 1 in 10 cars sold in the US being fully electric, introducing new security challenges.
- The security of EV charging systems and communication protocols is a growing concern, with vulnerabilities in authentication, data exchange, and charging infrastructure.
- Researchers have identified three classes of security risks: infiltration and control of energy flow, identity and data theft, and data manipulation.
- The Open Charge Point Protocol is widely used but has known vulnerabilities, and more secure protocols face technical and economic barriers to adoption.

### Detailed Points
- The EV industry's rapid growth has outpaced the development of secure charging infrastructure, creating a need for standardized security protocols.
- The authors of the paper surveyed real-world attacks, identified systemic weaknesses in widely deployed standards, and mapped out where current defenses are falling short.
- Modern EVs interface with energy networks, user data, and embedded automation tools, introducing vulnerabilities at multiple levels.
- The authors identified three classes of security risks:
  * Infiltration and control of energy flow: attackers can exploit digital interfaces to disrupt or reroute electricity flows.
  * Identity and data theft: EVs collect sensitive user data, which becomes vulnerable when storage or transmission protocols lack adequate security.
  * Data manipulation: data exchanged between the vehicle and the grid can be altered in man-in-the-middle attacks, potentially leading to mismanagement of battery health or unsafe driving conditions.
- Charging infrastructure is the most frequently compromised subsystem, with over 40% of documented attacks, due to weak authentication protocols and interaction with local energy distribution networks.
- Tampering and denial-of-service attacks are the most frequent, followed by man-in-the-middle attacks and data breaches, which exploit vulnerabilities in wireless communication links and controller area network bus modules.
- The authors evaluated communication protocols across two categories: front-end protocols between the vehicle and charging point, and back-end protocols between the charging point and external operators or systems.
- The ISO 15118 standard governs hardware and software best-practices for charging systems, but its implementation is ambiguous, particularly in wireless applications.
- The Open Charge Point Protocol dominates current implementations but has known vulnerabilities, and more secure protocols face technical and economic barriers to adoption.
- The authors reviewed various Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs), including those using deep neural networks, LSTMs, and GANs, but each has trade-offs in terms of detection rates, computational resources, and sensitivity to data quality.
- The industry is in need of standardization and technical leadership, with communication protocols widely deployed but unevenly hardened, and security mechanisms existing but inconsistently implemented.
- The paper's broader message is that EV charging infrastructure is currently scaling faster than its defensive architecture, and without coordinated standards and deliberate security design, this gap will only widen.

### Important Links
- **Read the Original Paper**: https://journalclub.io/track/EgcQDcyCZAkn1vh83vBAtJAxcvJbmW4LeouRdOL4efOBwk81hc (provides more details on protocol specifications, IDS performance, and suggested strategic framework)
- **Watch or Listen to the Episode**: https://journalclub.io/episodes/securing-the-ev-charging-ecosystem-protocol-level-vulnerabilities-defenses-and-a-research-roadmap?token=nCh7pLeYJ881dP5bunGnqCxkp4TH6L7TfmuxtqOHkrVoOS1lnN (discusses the methodology and analysis of the paper)

Securing the EV Charging Ecosystem: Protocol-Level Vulnerabilities, Defenses, and a Research Roadmap   

Over the past year, nearly 1 in 10 cars sold in the US were fully electric. If that number seems high, that's because it is. Spectacularly so. The ascension of the EV as a daily driver and passenger car has been nothing short of a step-change, and it took a lot of skeptics by surprise. It wasn't so long ago that programs like “Who Killed the Electric Car” were decrying the death of the entire industry, and searching for an explanation as to why it had come to such an untimely end. Quite the comeback story.

![](https://journalclub.io/px/l8eRBncWzjKqqRfUchmyCNBdzrbWfcmW5e1KPhEqBBJLpp4pWj)
